validation.summary: 6 defect(s) detected. Structural score: 1.000. Coverage score: 0.913. Hallucination score: 1.000. Semantic score: 1.000. Overall score: 0.913.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers most of the lifecycle, but it still misses several required behaviors and includes one unsupported behavior. The main gaps are around policy interaction details, load-distribution/content-replication requirements, and the exact termination/re-arrangement exception handling.

defects.description: The required exchange of policy, resource information, and service requirements with external PAs is not explicitly represented.
defects.evidence: R49 requires the Peering Agent to exchange policy, resource information, and service requirements with external PAs. The diagram has discovery/negotiation and protocol configuration, but no action that explicitly exchanges all three information types with external PAs.
defects.suggested_action: Add a Local Peering Agent action that explicitly exchanges policy, resource information, and service requirements with external PAs during negotiation/discovery.

defects.description: The cooperative pull-based content replication behavior is missing.
defects.evidence: R52 requires content replication using a cooperative pull-based approach where participating CDNs assist each other in serving data. The current diagram shows protocol setup, load exchange, and request redirection, but no explicit content replication step or cooperative pull-based replication behavior.
defects.suggested_action: Add an action for cooperative pull-based content replication between participating CDNs after peering is established.

defects.description: The mediator’s collection of up-to-date resource information from the Service Registry is not explicitly shown.
defects.evidence: R61 states that the Mediator collects up-to-date resource information from SR. The diagram includes a mediator action to get registry and policy data, but does not explicitly represent collection of up-to-date resource information from the Service Registry as required.
defects.suggested_action: Refine the mediator action so it explicitly collects up-to-date resource information from the Service Registry.

defects.description: The service-registration trigger conditions are incomplete because provider-startup registration is not explicitly modeled.
defects.evidence: R62 requires service registration to be triggered when resources are available as a provider starts operating, when existing information needs updating, during traffic surges, and when SR instances are created for established peering arrangements. The diagram models new/existing resource handling and traffic surge handling, but not the provider-starts-operating trigger explicitly.
defects.suggested_action: Add an explicit trigger/decision branch for service registration when a provider starts operating and resources become available.

defects.description: The peering-trigger condition does not explicitly consider both expected and unexpected load increases.
defects.evidence: R81 requires the triggering condition to consider expected and unexpected load increases in the initiating CDN. The diagram checks hotspot, timeout, and malicious request, but does not explicitly model expected versus unexpected load increase as part of the trigger condition.
defects.suggested_action: Revise the peering trigger decision to explicitly evaluate expected and unexpected load increases before sending the initialization request.

defects.description: The requirement that the WS sends the initialization request to the mediator is modeled, but the mediator-side receipt/generation path skips the explicit service-requirements-to-local-PA handoff condition for this trigger path.
defects.evidence: R87 requires the WS to send the initialization request, followed by mediator generation of service requirements and a conditional pass to the local PA. The diagram proceeds from receipt to requirements generation and policy check, but the conditional requirement that unacceptable requests must not be passed is not separated as a distinct branch tied to this specific trigger path.
defects.suggested_action: Split the mediator policy check so the acceptable path passes requirements to the local PA and the unacceptable path stops without passing them, with explicit linkage to the initiation request path.

defects.description: Malicious request handling is present, but it is not tied to a clearly identified and acted-upon discovery/negotiation behavior as required.
defects.evidence: R123 requires malicious requests to be identified and acted upon. The diagram includes a malicious-request decision and rejection action, but it is only attached as a side branch after policy/policy-policy handling, not as a clearly integrated discovery-time or request-handling behavior.
defects.suggested_action: Connect malicious-request detection and rejection directly to the relevant request-processing path where the malicious request is encountered.

defects.description: The diagram introduces a separate 'Deliver content to end-users based on negotiated policies' action that is not explicitly required as a standalone activity in this process model.
defects.evidence: The requirements describe content delivery, redirection, and policy-based control, but do not define a distinct standalone activity labeled as 'Deliver content to end-users based on negotiated policies' in this lifecycle diagram.
defects.suggested_action: If this action is intended only as a summary of redirection/delivery, merge it into the existing redirection/content-delivery flow rather than modeling it as a separate activity.

strengths: The diagram covers the major phases: service registration, initiation, negotiation, resource discovery, operational management, and disband/re-arrangement.
The service-registration path correctly includes new-resource registration, updates, traffic-surge supply, and failure removal behavior.
The mediator-to-PA negotiation chain is modeled with policy acceptance/rejection branching.
Operational management includes configuration advertising, load exchange, accounting, policy deployment, and refusal-based cessation.
The disband/re-arrangement section includes the termination-condition branch and an exceptional-circumstances bypass path.
missing_requirements: Explicit modeling of cooperative pull-based content replication between participating CDNs (R52).
Explicit mediator collection of up-to-date resource information from the Service Registry (R61).
Explicit provider-startup trigger for service registration when resources become available (R62).
Explicit consideration of expected vs. unexpected load increases in the peering trigger condition (R81).
Explicit exchange of policy, resource information, and service requirements with external PAs (R49).
unsupported_behaviors: A separate standalone 'Deliver content to end-users based on negotiated policies' activity is added without a distinct required lifecycle step named that way.
